title: Counting hypergraphs without linear cycles of fixed length
summary: Let $C_{k}^{(r)}$ be the $r$-uniform linear cycle on $k$ hyperedges. An $r$-graph is $C_{k}^{(r)}$-free if it contains no copy of $C_{k}^{(r)}$. Let $\operatorname{ex}_{r}(n,C_{k}^{(r)})$ denote the maximum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex $C_{k}^{(r)}$-free $r$-graph. Balogh, Narayanan and Skokan asked whether, for every pair of integers $r,k\ge 3$, the number of $C_k^{(r)}$-free $r$-graphs on $n$ labelled vertices is \[ 2^{(1+o(1))\operatorname{ex}_{r}(n,C_{k}^{(r)})}. \] While the analogous statement is known to fail for graphs ($r=2$), by a construction of Morris and Saxton, the…
